tweet_summary: Complex Pop Culture tweet asserting the Astrophage scene in 'Project Hail Mary' was shot practically, with two BTS images.
why_note_decision: The Astrophage close-ups in Project Hail Mary WERE shot practically — Lord/Miller used a chicken-wire rig with infrared LEDs, water poured between glass panes, and a full-spectrum ARRI ALEXA 65 with the IR filter removed (covered by GeekTyrant, SlashFilm, CinemaBlend, Yahoo, Kolari Vision, ScreenRant, and the directors themselves). Wide shots were augmented/replaced digitally by ILM, but the principal 'breathtaking Astrophage scene' the tweet refers to is the practical close-up work. The original note's claim that the scene was 'made entirely digitally by ILM' is incorrect.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet's claim that the Astrophage scene was shot practically is substantively true (close-ups used IR LEDs on chicken wire + water refraction, captured with a modified ALEXA 65; ILM did wides and augmentation). Any note that says it was 'made entirely digitally' or 'fully CGI' is a false positive. A note is only justified if it adds the nuance that wides were digital — but doing so contradicts the tweet's claim only weakly and was poorly received here.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The director states the Astrophage shots were made entirely digitally by ILM. https://x.com/chrizmillr/status/2037629284622233902 https://x.com/ILMVFX/status/2037793550096839031
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Factually wrong — the close-up Astrophage shots were practical (IR LEDs on chicken wire, water refraction, modified ALEXA 65). Only wides were fully digital. Misrepresents the director's own remarks.

fact_check.notes: Hybrid: close-ups practical (IR + chicken wire + water), wides digital by ILM. Tweet's 'shot practically' is correct for the famous Astrophage close-ups.

importance.lens_rationale: VFX trivia; minimal world-impact. Useful in eval as a 'note is wrong, tweet is right' false-positive case.
